toc.title: Provenance and Uncertainty in Multi-Source Synthesis (Task 5.6)

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. URL: uniform resource locator

  • Why an overall accuracy figure can hide weak spots
  • Stratified random sampling and field-level confidence calibrated on a labeled validation set
  • Routing documents to human reviewers when capacity is limited
  • Claim-source mappings, conflicting values, dates and fitting the format to the content

2Human Review and Confidence Calibration (Task 5.5)

Running case

Birchwood Supply Automates Invoice Entry

  • The extraction system reports 97% accuracy overall, so management wants to stop most human review
  • Closer inspection shows handwritten receipts at only 70% and the tax-ID field often wrong
  • Reviewers can check only a few hundred documents a week
Principle Detail
Aggregate accuracy hides problems 97% overall can mask poor performance on specific document types or fields
Validate by segment Measure accuracy by document type and by field before automating high-confidence extractions or reducing review
Stratified random sampling Keep sampling high-confidence extractions from each segment: it measures the true error rate and detects novel error patterns
Field-level confidence Have the model output a confidence per field, then calibrate thresholds on a labeled validation set (compare confidence to real correctness)
Routing Send low-confidence, ambiguous or contradictory-source extractions to people; prioritize limited reviewer capacity where errors are most likely

  • Why sampling the confident ones matters: a threshold chosen once can drift as documents change; random samples show it.
  • Raw model confidence is not a calibrated probability. It becomes useful only after you compare it with ground truth on labeled data and set thresholds from that.
Exam tip

"Accuracy is 97%, so reduce review" → check accuracy per document type and field first, and keep stratified sampling.

Exam tip

Confidence scores are useful only after calibration on a labeled validation set.

3Provenance and Uncertainty in Multi-Source Synthesis (Task 5.6)

Case (continued): Birchwood's research system reports two market-size figures: $4.1 billion from an industry association (2022 data) and $5.3 billion from an analyst firm (2025 data). The first draft report quietly uses $5.3 billion and drops the other.

Problem Remedy
Source attribution is lost when findings are compressed in summaries Require structured claim-source mappings (claim, source URL, document name, relevant excerpt) that the synthesis agent preserves and merges
Conflicting statistics from credible sources Annotate the conflict with source attribution; do not arbitrarily pick one. Let the coordinator decide how to reconcile
Dates ignored Require publication or data-collection dates in structured outputs, so a temporal difference of years is not misinterpreted as a contradiction
Everything in one format Render each content type appropriately: financial data as tables, news as prose, technical findings as structured lists
Established vs disputed claims blended Use explicit sections that separate well-established findings from contested ones, keeping the original source characterizations and methodological context

  • The document analysis subagent should finish its work with the conflicting values included and annotated and pass them on, rather than resolving the conflict silently.
Exam tip

Two credible sources disagree → keep both with attribution (and dates); never "pick the most recent" or "average them" without a stated basis.

4Exam Q&A

S1Invoice extraction shows 97% accuracy overall, and management wants to remove most human review. What should the team do first?

  • ARemove review for all documents
  • BRaise the model temperature
  • CAnalyze accuracy by document type and by field before reducing review
  • DReview only the lowest-confidence document each day
Show the answer

Answer: C. Aggregate accuracy can hide weak segments; validate per type and field first.

S2How can a team keep detecting new error patterns in extractions that the model rates as high confidence?

  • ATake stratified random samples of high-confidence extractions
  • BReview only the five oldest items
  • CStop looking at high-confidence items
  • DReview only the items that already failed validation in the pipeline
Show the answer

Answer: A. Sampling across segments measures error rates and uncovers novel failure patterns.

S3Model-reported field confidence scores exist, but nobody knows what "0.85" means in practice. How should review thresholds be set?

  • AUse 0.5 for everything
  • BChoose a threshold randomly
  • CCalibrate thresholds on a labeled validation set by comparing confidence with correctness
  • DUse the highest confidence score ever seen as the single review threshold for every field
Show the answer

Answer: C. Calibration against labeled ground truth turns raw scores into useful routing thresholds.

S4Reviewer capacity is limited. Which routing rule is best?

  • AReview a random 10% of everything
  • BSend low-confidence, ambiguous or contradictory extractions to review first
  • CSend documents in alphabetical order
  • DReview only the documents that come from the biggest supplier of the company
Show the answer

Answer: B. Concentrate scarce attention on the items most likely to be wrong.

S5Two reputable sources give different market sizes, one with 2022 data and one with 2025 data. What should the report do?

  • APresent both values with their sources and dates, annotating the conflict
  • BUse the newer figure and omit the older
  • CRemove the topic
  • DAverage the two
Show the answer

Answer: A. Preserve both values with attribution and dates; the dates may explain the difference.

S6Which TWO steps are needed before reducing human review of automated extraction? Select TWO.

  • AChoose a single threshold at random
  • BStop all review at once
  • CRely on the overall accuracy figure only
  • DKeep stratified random sampling of confident extractions
  • EMeasure accuracy by document type and field
Show the answer

Answer: D, E. Segment-level accuracy and ongoing sampling show where the system is weak. An overall number can hide poor segments.

S7Which TWO practices handle conflicting statistics from credible sources correctly? Select TWO.

  • AInclude publication or collection dates
  • BKeep both values with their sources
  • CDrop the older value
  • DPick the largest value
  • EAverage the values without saying so
Show the answer

Answer: A, B. Both values with attribution and dates let readers judge; the dates may explain the difference.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Aggregate accuracy Can hide poor document types or fields → validate by segment first
Sampling Stratified random samples of high-confidence output → true error rate, novel patterns
Confidence Field-level; calibrate on a labeled validation set
Routing Low confidence, ambiguity, contradictions → people; prioritize limited capacity
Provenance Claim-source mappings (URL, document, excerpt) preserved through synthesis
Conflicts Keep both values with attribution; coordinator decides; never pick arbitrarily
Dates Require publication/collection dates (time differences are not contradictions)
Rendering Finance → tables · news → prose · technical findings → structured lists; separate established from contested
